en.title: Box OA #1: Identifying Counterfeit Coins
en.input: The first line contains n; each of the next n lines contains a serial number. 0<n≤100000, 1≤serial number length≤14, and serial numbers contain only English letters and digits.
en.output: Output one integer: 99% of the total denomination of the valid coins, rounded down.
en.explanation:
Example 1: the valid coins are AVG190420T (20), RTF20001000Z (1000), ERT1947200T (200), and DRV1984500Y (500), totaling 1720; after deducting 1% it is 1702.8, which rounds down to 1702. QWER201850G has an R in the year position; the first three letters of AFA199620E are not distinct; RTY20202004 has an out-of-range year and its last character is not an uppercase letter; ETB2010400G uses a 400 denomination, which does not exist.
Example 2: 100×0.99=99.
Example 3: three coins of 10 total 30, which is 29.7 after the fee, rounded down to 29.
hints: The denomination lies between the 8th character and the 2nd-to-last character.
Compare the denomination against the set of denominations with exact string comparison.
The fee is computed once on the total of the whole transaction.
